ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, in the circuit, $R_{1}$, $R_{2}$, and $R_{3}$ are fixed resistors with a resistance of $4\Omega$ each. A constant voltage of 6V is applied across terminals $a$ and $b$.

1. If $c$ and $d$ are connected to an ideal ammeter, what is the reading $I$ of the ammeter?
2. If $c$ and $d$ are connected to an ideal voltmeter, what is the reading $U$ of the voltmeter?
3. If a capacitor with $C=1.5\times10^{5}\mathrm{F}$ is connected to terminals $c$ and $d$, what is the charge $Q$ on the capacitor after the circuit has stabilized?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows terminal a on the upper left connected through resistor R1 to a central upper junction. From that junction, resistor R2 goes to terminal c on the upper right. Resistor R3 goes vertically downward from the same central upper junction to a lower node. The lower node is connected by a wire to terminal b on the lower left and terminal d on the lower right. Each resistor is 4 Ω, and 6 V is applied across a and b. Reasoning: 1. With an ideal ammeter connected between c and d, c and d are shorted. Then R2 connects from the central upper junction to the lower node, just like R3, so R2 and R3 are in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is 4 Ω || 4 Ω = 2 Ω. This is in series with R1 = 4 Ω, so the total resistance is 6 Ω and the source current is 6 V / 6 Ω = 1 A. The voltage across the parallel part is 1 A × 2 Ω = 2 V, so the current through R2, and therefore through the ammeter, is 2 V / 4 Ω = 0.5 A. 2. With an ideal voltmeter connected between c and d, the c-d branch is open, so no current flows through R2 and there is no voltage drop across R2. Thus c is at the same potential as the central upper junction. Only R1 and R3 are in series across 6 V; since they are equal resistors, each has a 3 V drop. Therefore the voltage between c and d is 3 V. 3. With a capacitor connected between c and d, after the circuit stabilizes under DC, the capacitor branch behaves as an open circuit. The final voltage across the capacitor is therefore the same as in the voltmeter case, 3 V. Hence Q = CU = (1.5×10^5 F)(3 V) = 4.5×10^5 C.
